key_insight: Time-modulated, spatially uniform heating can stabilize a microgravity liquid mirror by driving oscillatory thermocapillary flows that counteract the destabilizing effects of steady heating.
engineering_relevance: This provides a control strategy for large space telescopes and other thin liquid-surface systems, enabling meter-scale shape stability over multi-day timescales.
method: Built a long-wave model for a thin liquid mirror in microgravity.
Applied multiple-scale analysis to derive coupled surface-temperature evolution across many heating cycles.
Used linear stability analysis and numerical simulation to predict decay times and stability thresholds for surface modes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that numerical simulations validate the analytical predictions and show stabilization of meter-scale surface deformations over timescales of days.
watch_item: The approach relies on idealized model assumptions and controlled thermal modulation, so real spacecraft implementation may be sensitive to imperfect heating uniformity and disturbances.
paper_title: Thermocapillary stabilization of Liquid Space Telescopes
